D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The docs do not publish tool annotations. The documented validation/calculation/schema and polling tools are read-like; generate_tax_pdf_tool starts an asynchronous job and returns an ID, so it has a server-side effect. 2. No server-enforced confirmation or approval step is documented. Docs recommend checking inputs before calculation/PDF generation; Aiwyn says outputs remain subject to firm review and approval. 3. Claude lists sign-in as not required. No OAuth scopes, role inheritance, admin switches at Aiwyn, allowlists, token lifetime or revocation details were found. 4. No read-only mode, tool filter, alternate environment or regional endpoint is documented. 5. Aiwyn recommends anonymized/redacted/test data; it says it does not store firm or client data from Claude sessions. No field masking or server-enforced PII exclusion is documented. 6. Docs state support across federal and 43 state jurisdictions and async PDF generation; no rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, time caps or call costs published. 7. Docs prescribe wrapped values, whole-dollar currency, UUIDv4 array entries, UUIDv5 extended links, cross-references and date/ZIP/SSN patterns. They warn invalid extended-link UUIDs can cause silent data loss. Wire-level rejection/correction behavior is not documented. 8. Logging, audit trails and telemetry behavior are not described. Aiwyn says it does not store data from Claude sessions. 9. No feedback/rating/report/survey tool appears in the official list. The official blog describes vendor benefits and planned product direction; no upsell result or marketing elicitation tool is documented. 10. Workflow/input instructions are documentation text; server enforcement is not established. 11. No memory or state affecting future outputs is described, other than PDF job polling by ID. 12. The published interface is one server and one flat list of ten tools. 13. No raw API, SQL, script or arbitrary execution tool appears in the published list.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The connector does not file or e-file returns, provide a production workflow, or deliver returns to clients; Aiwyn says these are outside the current connector. Firms must review, approve and deliver outputs. The vendor separately markets tax filing APIs, but those are a distinct product surface, not connector tools.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The published workflow recommends calling tax_simple_return first, retrieving schemas, validating with check_tax, calculating, then generating and polling for the PDF. It advises whole-dollar integer amounts, wrapped field values, UUIDv4 for list entries and UUIDv5 for extended links. The docs do not establish that these recommendations are enforced server-side.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Aiwyn says: “Aiwyn does not store firm or client data from Claude sessions, or access your internal systems through this Connector.” It recommends anonymized, redacted or test data and says outputs remain subject to firm review and approval. Its article describes the current connector as exploratory and not a production workflow.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The docs describe a tax calculation pipeline for federal and single-state returns, with schema discovery, validation, calculation and downloadable PDF generation. Aiwyn frames its calculation layer as deterministic and verifiable.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented tool sequence is partially reflected by separate tools, including validation and calculation, but enforcement of sequence, data minimization, review, approval, storage claims and audit controls is not established by the public tool reference. No code or server implementation was available to verify these claims.

contradictions: The input describes the endpoint as unpublished/non-concrete, and the supplied OAuth note says metadata was not fetched on that basis; Anthropic's connector directory publishes https://mcp.columnapi.com/mcp as the connector URL. OAuth metadata for that published URL is absent from the supplied evidence.
The official docs list 10 tools including get_tax_pdf_tool; Anthropic's connector listing lists 9 and omits get_tax_pdf_tool.

Some third-party listings describe the connector as read-only, while the official docs say generate_tax_pdf_tool starts an asynchronous PDF-generation job. That operation creates a job, although the docs do not say it changes a tax return.
observations_for_research: The documented workflow divides preparation into discovery/schema retrieval, validation, calculation, and asynchronous PDF generation with polling.

The tool interface exposes schema and workflow guidance that can steer agent sequencing, while several data-shape rules and the firm review recommendation are documentation instructions whose server enforcement is not shown.
State-to-federal extended-link matching depends on deterministic UUIDv5 values; the docs warn that incorrect UUIDs may silently result in data loss.
